questions.prompt: What main claim does Chapter 6 make about discipline?
choices: Success requires perfect discipline in every area
Success depends on selective discipline around the right behavior
Discipline only matters in work settings

explanation.gentle: The chapter says total discipline is the wrong target and that narrower consistency matters more.
explanation.direct: Keller rejects universal self-control in favor of leveraged discipline.
explanation.competitive: Total control is fake. Hold the hinge.

questions.prompt: Why does Keller call the disciplined-life fantasy a lie?
choices: Because no routines should exist
Because total life control is treated as a prerequisite when it is not
Because discipline always becomes selfish

explanation.gentle: The chapter says people often treat perfect discipline as necessary before progress can begin, and that standard is false.
explanation.direct: Universal self-control is admired too much and leveraged too little.
explanation.competitive: The fantasy looks noble and still misses the result.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter's preferred alternative to total discipline?
choices: Selective consistency around one leveraged behavior
Waiting for more motivation
Redesigning every habit at once but more slowly

explanation.gentle: The chapter favors one repeated support routine that protects the One Thing.
explanation.competitive: Hold the hinge, not the whole fantasy.

questions.prompt: Tessa keeps rebuilding her whole schedule but never protects the opening block for the key project. What fits Chapter 6 best?
choices: Keep improving the whole day until it feels perfect
Wait until all surrounding habits are fixed first
Protect one repeatable start ritual for the important task

explanation.gentle: The chapter says one stable support routine can matter more than a full-system redesign.
explanation.competitive: Hold the block that moves the project.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would Chapter 6 reject as false?
choices: A person may need one reliable routine more than a perfectly optimized life
Meaningful progress cannot begin until every area of life is disciplined
Discipline should be aimed where it protects consequence

explanation.gentle: The chapter rejects the idea that universal discipline must arrive before progress can begin.
explanation.direct: Total control is not the entry fee.

questions.prompt: Julian built a broad study overhaul but never held one stable review block for the hardest class. What did Chapter 6 say he missed?
choices: The need for a bigger planning system
The value of complete life control
The leverage of one support routine around the hinge course

explanation.gentle: One recurring review block would have protected the class carrying the most consequence.
explanation.direct: He missed selective discipline around the hinge.
explanation.competitive: The system looked serious and left the key class loose.

questions.prompt: What limit keeps Chapter 6 from becoming an excuse for disorder?
choices: Selective discipline means structure still matters outside the chosen routine
Only personal life needs discipline
One good habit cancels the rest of the mess

explanation.gentle: The chapter says selective discipline is not permission for chaos everywhere else.
explanation.direct: Narrow structure is not the same as careless living.
explanation.competitive: One hinge does not excuse the wreckage.

questions.prompt: Mina argues that one weekly family reset matters more than becoming disciplined about everything at once. What is the best Chapter 6 response?
choices: She should wait for a full domestic system first
Any smaller routine is automatically lazy
One recurring reset can protect the load-bearing responsibility better than total perfectionism

explanation.gentle: The chapter favors the routine that stabilizes what matters most.
explanation.direct: Protect the hinge before worshiping total order.
explanation.competitive: Feed the reset that holds the week.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 6 build on Chapter 5?
choices: It explains how protected attention becomes sustainable through a narrower support routine
It abandons sequence and returns to multitasking
It says attention no longer matters once discipline appears

explanation.gentle: Chapter 5 protects one line of effort, and Chapter 6 explains how chosen discipline helps that protection hold.
explanation.direct: Sequence needs support structure if it is going to last.
explanation.competitive: After the blur dies, the hinge needs a routine.

questions.prompt: Which action best applies Chapter 6 to a crowded life?
choices: Build a perfect system for every domain before starting
Choose the one repeated routine that most protects the important result
Keep changing several habits until the whole life feels disciplined

explanation.gentle: The chapter works when discipline is concentrated on the behavior with the strongest consequence.
explanation.direct: Protect the routine that guards the result.
explanation.competitive: Hold the hinge and stop polishing the machine.
